en: The Apadāna of the Elder Sumanabījaniya Naḷamāli Chapter 4.4 I was a young man named Sumanas, A master of the three Vedas, skilled in the six branches. I was a teacher of the Vedas, Wise, learned, and well-versed in the scriptures. At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, The Teacher, arrived at Rājagaha. Having heard of the arrival of the Buddha, The Teacher, the most excellent of men, I went to the presence of the Buddha, With a mind full of faith and joy. There I saw the Buddha, the Blessed One, Seated upon a seat of kusa grass. Seeing him, my heart was filled with joy, And I offered a fan made of flowers. Because of that meritorious deed, For eighty-four thousand aeons, I never fell into the lower realms, But always dwelt in the heavenly worlds. In my final existence here, I was born into a noble family. When I attained the age of maturity, I renounced the world and went forth. Having gone forth, I practiced the holy life, And realized the state of an arahant. Through this very same wholesome deed, I have become a recipient of offerings. May all beings be well and happy; May no harm come to anyone. May all see what is auspicious; May none encounter misfortune. Thus ends the Apadāna of the Elder Sumanabījaniya.
“Sumana, taking a fan, approached the supreme Bodhi tree of the Blessed One Vipassī.”
I do not recognize a state of woe;
this is the fruit of sowing seeds.
The defilements have been burnt away by me.
Welcome indeed has come to me!
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
The four analytical knowledges (paṭisambhidā) are attained.
the Buddha’s teaching has been fulfilled.
Thus indeed did the Venerable Elder Sumanabījaniyo speak these verses.
The legend of the Elder Sumanabījaniya is the fourth.
